title: Thermostat Rationality / Coolant Temp Low
meaning: Engine coolant does not reach target operating temperature within calculated engine run time (typically due to stuck-open plastic thermostat).
symptoms: Cabin heater warm but not hot
Check Engine Light on
Temperature gauge stays in lower third
inspectionSteps: Feel upper radiator hose warmth immediately upon starting cold engine.
Inspect plastic thermostat housing neck for hairline cracks or pink coolant crust.
Read live Coolant Temp Telemetry.
verifiedFixes: Replace complete Thermostat and Housing assembly (OEM Mopar with integrated gasket)
Bleed air from cooling system via bleeder screw on Pentastar housing

title: Multiple Cylinder Misfire / Pentastar Camshaft Wear
meaning: Crankshaft speed fluctuations indicate combustion failure. On 3.6L Pentastar engines, frequently caused by failed rocker arm needle bearings wearing down the camshaft lobe.
symptoms: Audible rapid metallic ticking / sewing machine sound from cylinder head
Flashing Check Engine Light under acceleration
Rough idle
inspectionSteps: Remove valve cover and inspect camshaft lobes for grooving or gouges.
Inspect rocker arm roller bearings for excessive play or seized needle bearings.
Inspect spark plugs and ignition coil boots.
verifiedFixes: Replace worn camshaft and rocker arm assembly on affected bank (Pentastar common failure)
Replace spark plugs and ignition coils

title: EVAP System Very Small Leak (.020")
meaning: PCM failed evaporative system natural vacuum leak detection test (NVLD / ESIM switch did not close during cool-down).
symptoms: Check Engine Light on
'gascap' warning illuminated on odometer display
inspectionSteps: Inspect gas cap rubber O-ring seal for dirt or cracks.
Locate Evaporative System Integrity Module (ESIM) mounted on charcoal canister near fuel tank.
Lightly tap ESIM switch body or inspect its rubber connecting boot for dry-rot.
verifiedFixes: Replace ESIM / NVLD switch assembly on charcoal canister (80% common fix)
Replace gas cap with OEM Mopar cap
Replace cracked EVAP vapor line near purge solenoid

title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor / Switch Circuit Malfunction
meaning: PCM detected out-of-range voltage on the dual-stage engine oil pressure sensor circuit. Very common on 3.2L/3.6L Pentastar V6 and 5.7L HEMI engines.
symptoms: Check Engine Light on
EVIC displays 'Oil Pressure Sensor Error' or pegged 99 PSI / 0 PSI
Remote start inoperative
inspectionSteps: Check live engine oil pressure telemetry with ignition on / engine off (should read 0 PSI; failing sensors read 40-90 PSI key-off).
Inspect oil filter housing valley under lower intake manifold for oil puddling.
Inspect wiring harness to sensor at rear of oil cooler adapter.
verifiedFixes: Replace faulty Engine Oil Pressure Sensor on rear of oil cooler assembly
Replace complete plastic Pentastar oil filter adapter assembly with upgraded aluminum unit if leaking

title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor / Switch Low Voltage
meaning: Oil pressure signal wire voltage dropped below 0.2V (indicating internal sensor diaphragm rupture or open ground).
symptoms: Oil can warning icon on instrument cluster
Check Engine Light on
Low oil pressure chime
inspectionSteps: Verify engine oil level on dipstick immediately before cranking.
Listen for valvetrain clicking / ticking (confirms mechanical oil pressure).
Measure sensor reference voltage (5V) and signal return.
verifiedFixes: Replace oil pressure sensor (OEM Mopar recommended to avoid calibration drift)
Check oil filter cap bypass valve spring

inspectionSteps: Check engine oil viscosity: MDS strictly requires 5W-20 (5.7L) or 0W-40 (6.4L); incorrect viscosity prevents hydraulic lifters from locking.

Replace failing MDS Solenoid under intake manifold

title: Lost Communication with ECM/PCM / Dual Battery Variance
meaning: TCM, BCM, or ABS lost CAN bus heartbeat from Powertrain Control Module. Very common on 2018+ Jeep Wrangler/Gladiator and Ram with dual ESS (Engine Stop-Start) batteries.
symptoms: Start-Stop warning message on dash
Random cluster lights blinking
Intermittent no-crank / no-start
inspectionSteps: Test AUX auxiliary battery health (small 12V battery under main battery tray or fender). A weak AUX battery drags down main CAN bus voltage.
Inspect TIPM / PDC fuse box connectors for corrosion.
Verify main chassis ground stud next to battery.

Clean and reseat TIPM power distribution block connectors
